summary.text: Shelley Kloba is a Democratic member of the Washington House of Representatives for District 1-Position 2, in office since January 9, 2017, and she is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Republican Cliff Moon.
She came to the Legislature after work as a parent advocate in her daughter's public schools, service as Washington State PTA Legislative Director and a term on the Kirkland City Council.

paragraphs.text: Kloba's House Democratic biography says her path to the Legislature began as a parent advocate at her daughter's public schools.
She served a four-year term on the Kirkland Park Board and as a trustee for the Lake Washington School Foundation, and in 2011 she was elected Washington State PTA Legislative Director.
She was then appointed and elected to the Kirkland City Council, where she served from 2013 to 2016.

Kloba graduated from the University of Illinois with a B.S. in kinesiology in 1990 and from the Seattle Massage School with honors in 1996, and she earned a certificate in Energy Policy Planning from the University of Idaho in 2017.
Kloba was elected to her first term in the House in November 2016.

Her House Democratic biography lists her as vice chair of the Technology, Economic Development, & Veterans Committee and a member of the Consumer Protection & Business and Environment & Energy committees.

She has taken a lead role on gambling policy, including a 2019 law creating a voluntary program that lets people with a gambling disorder exclude themselves from gambling at multiple venues, and she sponsors the People's Privacy Act on data privacy.
